set.approach: From the ski area, park in the upper lot behind the lodge and walk up the paved McCollister Road toward the Union Pass lift. Where the pavement stops a small trail leaves to the left; it meets a service road, which you follow left until it turns into a steep trail climbing to the buttress. Climbers using the tram instead descend by the Rock Springs Loop trail along the ridge opposite Cody Peak, bear left on the road at the first junction, take the trail down to the next junction and turn right toward the ski trails, then pick up a cairned climbers' trail on the right that drops to the base. The West Sector is the far-left crag after the creek, on the talus field, with a steep gully on its right, and it is the first crag reached when coming down from the tram.

set.approach: Pull off into the small parking spot on the left side of Hinkey Summit Road, short of the bend. Walk up the road a short way to two cairns on the right marking the trail, then head north-northeast on the best cow trail across the hillside. Cross Indian Creek at the stick-and-rock cairn by a large Y-shaped dead snag, then follow cow and climber trails along the treeline northeast until the wall appears over the crest. The west side of the formation is the steeper, pocketed face; the south side is lower angle.

set.approach: From the upper climbers' camp, take the trail down across Forest Service Road 850 and climb the Lookout Ridge Trail until just short of the crest of the Panorama Point knoll, where a side trail leaves on the left onto the point (Rabbit Ears is close by to the south); follow it down the left (back) side of the point to the base of the cliff.

set.approach: Park where the seasonal road from Route 108 ends and walk up the road; the cliffs stand on both sides of it. The buttress is a clean wall just south of the Quartz Crack Face. Starting at Quartz Crack, contour north (to the right, facing the rock) and a little downhill past The Diagonal to a low-angle bolted slab, with the climbs just right of the herd path. Other ways in: climb south on the herd path out of ENT Gully, or head straight up from the top of the Smugglers' Notch lot past Biscuit.

set.approach: Drive up Little Cottonwood Canyon to Tanners Campground and park on the large shoulder on the east side just past it, before the bend. Behind the Tanners Slide Path sign across the highway a trail leads down to the drainage; follow it into the gulch and walk up the drainage (the west side of the stream seems to have the better trail). Look for the first pronounced gully on the left, Witches and Divas; the east-facing wall is on the right side of that gully. The upper gulch is steep with loose talus, and it is avalanche terrain in winter and spring, so check the avalanche forecast.

Climb the switchbacks above Wall Lake to Hope Lake, follow its east side to the pass, go by Lake Lovenia and descend switchbacks to Ibantik Lake. The north-facing wall is south of the lake: walk up talus on the west side and skirt the base of the cliff to your route.

set.approach: Follow the approach to the Shattered Sea (see that crag), then keep going toward the cliff edge. The trail skirts the edge over broken rock and short cliffs, then slopes downhill and opens out with less deadfall. When the ground begins to rise again, watch for a cluster of cairns on your right by some pines, which mark the crag top. The base is reached by a short, steep talus chute, which is best roped.

set.approach: From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow and turn left, then follow the two-track to parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of the fence heading southeast, through a short stretch of dense deadfall. A little past the deadfall find the first break on the left, marked by a small cairn, and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff edge. A cairned trail then continues southeast to the crag, though it can be hard to follow in places. The north entrance to the crag is marked by two cairns.

Walk the old logging road left of the fence heading southeast, through a short stretch of dense deadfall. A little past the deadfall find the first break on the left, marked by a small cairn, and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff edge. A cairned trail then continues southeast to the crag, though it can be hard to follow in places. The north entrance to the crag is marked by two cairns.
